Kailāsa
------------------------------------------
Kailāsa has been mentioned in the Rāmāyaṇa, the Mahābhārata and some Purānas as the abode or world of शिव. It is one of the northern peaks of the हिमालयस्. It is also called Rajatādri (= the mountain of silver).
Mt. KailāsDevotees of शिव who get लिबेरतिओन् are believed to go to this world.
The Pāṇḍavas had visited this place during their पिल्ग्रिमगे while living in exile in the forest.
According to the Śivapurāṇa कृष्ण is said to have performed austerities here to please शिव.
Alakāpurī, the capital of कुबेर was also situated in this peak.
Rāvaṇa had once tried to uproot it with his twenty hands but was severely punished by शिव who just pressed his big toe and got him trapped!
The modern कैलास mountain is about 40 kms. (25 miles) from the famous Mānasa Sarovara in Tibet.

Kailāsanatha Temple
------------------------------------------
See ELLORA.
There is a Kailāsanātha Temple at काञ्चीपुरम् also. See KĀÑCĪPURAM for details.
